discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, founding twistronics and moiré quantum matter

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré superlattices and strongly correlated two-dimensional materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted by a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees would have nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers confirmed this. With precisely controlled twisted, gated heterostructures they found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity whose phase diagram resembles those of the cuprates. The twist angle thus became a new control knob for quantum matter. The platform is clean, tunable in situ by gate voltage, and made from simple components. Hundreds of groups quickly adopted it, and it has since yielded correlated magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, Wigner crystals and Mott states in transition-metal-dichalcogenide moirés, and fractional Chern insulators without a magnetic field. The theory's conceptual clarity and the experiment's elegance changed what physicists can build and measure in low-dimensional many-body systems.
